agent: wave 2 agent A (trigger leaves: country and diplomacy)
question: What each country and diplomacy trigger leaf's Evaluate (slot 6) answers, with scope part, missing-scope, comparison, THIS/FROM and null-name behaviour.

addresses.name: CIsAiTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CIsAiTrigger's table (rva 0x11F8B88), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end. `cmp [ecx+eax*4], ebx(0); sete al; cmp al, [edi+0x40]; sete al` at 0x5ED456-0x5ED469. Wrong if +0xBCC were a by-value array - it is loaded first (`mov ecx,[ecx+0xbcc]`) and then indexed.

addresses.name: CCanCreateVassalsTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`can_create_vassals`: the scope's country has at least one releasable nation - and the value is never read.** 0x5EE030 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5EE063.

    return CCountry::GetPossibleVassals(countries[scope->country_id])->count (+8) > 0

`this` (ECX) is overwritten at 0x5EE03C before any read, so **`can_create_vassals = no` answers exactly as `= yes`**. GetPossibleVassals (0xEE320) rebuilds CCountry +0x11E0 on every call, so this allocates.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CCanCreateVassalsTrigger's table (rva 0x11F8C24), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; the whole body is 13 instructions; no `[ecx+0x40]` or `[edi+0x40]` read exists in it. Wrong if a caller passed the value some other way - slot 6 has one stack argument (`ret 4`) and that is the scope.

addresses.name: CCasusBelliTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CCasusBelliTrigger's table (rva 0x11F887C), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end; the three pushes before the call at 0x5E7CD3 are &other (lea [esp+8]), scope+0x10, and the status. Wrong if 0x649CA0 took its arguments in another order - its body uses [ebp+8] as the status (passes it on to 0x649D80, which walks its +0x3C), [ebp+0xC] as the holder and [ebp+0x10] as the target.

addresses.name: CDateTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`date = Y.M.D`: `now + scope->days_in_month (+0x34) * 24 >= this->date (+0x40)`**, in hours. 0x5D3100 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D31B8; game state get-or-create inlined.

    return state->tick (+0xBDC) + scope->+0x34 * 24 >= this->date

**This is the reader of CEventScope +0x34 the record lacked.** RunDailyEventPass leaves +0x34 at 0, so there `date` is an exact 'on or after'; RebuildCountryEventCandidates sets it to the current month's length, so in the candidate pass `date` is already true up to 28-31 days early - an event dated within the coming month is admitted as a candidate and the daily pass then tests it exactly. That purpose is inference; the arithmetic is read. `year` (0x5D2510) and `month` (0x5D2B30) do not read +0x34.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CDateTrigger's table (rva 0x11F7D50), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; `mov eax,[eax+0x34]; mov ecx,[ecx+0xbdc]; lea edx,[eax+eax*2]; lea ecx,[ecx+edx*8]; cmp ecx,[edi+0x40]; setge al` at 0x5D3192-0x5D31AA - edx*8 with edx = 3*eax is 24*eax. Control: the year/month bodies decoded end to end show `+0xBDC` and no `+0x34`.

addresses.name: CFactionTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`faction = <name>`: the scope's country is in that (real) faction.** 0x5FC8E0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5FC960 and 0x5FC96B, one frame.

    if (scope->country_id == 0) return false          // the only leaf of this set that tests it
    f = this->faction (+0x40)
    if (arg_is_this (+0x18)) f = countries[EventScope_GetCountryTag(scope).id]->faction (+0xD8)
    if (f == 0 || !f->slot7()) return false            // slot 7: ReturnTrue on CFaction, ReturnFalse on CNullFaction
    return countries[scope->country_id]->faction == f

So `faction = THIS` is 'the scope and THIS share a real faction'; an unknown name and `faction = FROM` (looked up as a name) give CNullFaction and are false. arg_is_from is never read.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CFactionTrigger's table (rva 0x11F8334), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end; `vtable.py CFaction CNullFaction` shows slot 7 = 0x692590 (ReturnTrue) against 0x192360 (ReturnFalse). Wrong if a country's faction could be CNullFaction-but-real - it cannot, slot 7 is the only difference tested.

An unknown name leaves +0x40 null and is false for every country whose government pointer is set. No THIS/FROM, no test for country 0.

addresses.name: CGuaranteeTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`guarantee = TAG` is an inlined copy of CDiplomacyStatus::IsGuaranting (0x648730)** on the scope's status toward TAG. 0x5F8BB0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F8C39 and 0x5F8C43.

    THIS is EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40) - this_scope's country, or the owner of this_scope's province when it has none; FROM is `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country (+0x18/+0x1C)`; otherwise the tag at +0x40/+0x44 (CTagTrigger's). 
    s = us->diplomacy (+0xE28) [other.id]; g = s->guarantee (+0x1C)
    return g != 0 && g->first.id (+0xC) != s->Target.id (+0xC)

True when a guarantee exists between the pair and TAG is **not** its first party - i.e. the scope's country is. The game's own Lua name for the same test, IsGuaranting, says the scope country is the guarantor; that direction is the name's, not read off a writer.

addresses.name: CHasCasusBelliTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`has_cb = { type = T actor = A }` asks about war goals, not casus belli: does a country at war with the scope's country hold a war goal of type T against it.** 0x5E8410 to two `ret 4` at 0x5E853A and 0x5E8696 (one frame, SEH slot shared).

    db = the casus-belli-type database g_casus_belli_types (0x1685BD8), made on first use
    t  = CMessageHandler::LookupType(db@EAX, &this->type (+0x48))   // 0x299AC0, by name, every evaluation
    if (t == 0) t = db->+0xC[0]                                      // index 0, the CNullCasusBelliType
    if (t == 0 || !t->slot7()) { log 'Error in has_cb trigger - invalid CB type!' (trigger.cpp 0xA29, channel 0x10004); return false }
    actor = HasCbTrigger_ResolveActor(this, scope)                    // 0x5E83C0: THIS/FROM off this_scope, else +0x40/+0x44
    if (actor.id && us->diplomacy[actor.id]->war (+0x20))
        for g in War_GetGoalsOf(war, actor)                           // 0x652410, CWar +0x9C
            if (g->receiver.id (+0x24) == scope->country_id && g->casus_belli (+0xC)->index (+8) == t->index (+8)) return true
    for e in us->enemies (+0x1008)                                    // every country at war with us
        if (e.id && countries[e.id]->owned_province_count (+0xCF8) > 0 && us->diplomacy[e.id]->war)
            same test on War_GetGoalsOf(that war, e)
    return false

**`actor` restricts nothing**: when the actor's goals do not match, every enemy is tried anyway, the actor among them. The only case it changes is an actor at war with the scope that owns no province, which the fall-back skips. An unknown `type` is logged on every evaluation and is false.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CHasCasusBelliTrigger's table (rva 0x11F88B0), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end (0x290 bytes to slot 8 at 0x5E86A0). ESI at both 0x652410 calls is the status's +0x20 (0x5E84E9, 0x5E858C). CWarGoal +0x20/+0x24 is `receiver` and +0xC `casus_belli` in the record; CWarGoal::AddToWar files a goal under its actor's id in CWar +0x9C. Wrong if the enemies list held countries not at war - it is rebuilt from `+0x20 != 0` by UpdateAtWarAndEnemies, and the war test is repeated here anyway.

addresses.name: CHasCountryModifierTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`has_country_modifier = <name>`: some entry of the scope's country's active_modifiers (+0x648) has this modifier.** 0x5E3320 to two `ret 4` at 0x5E3364 and 0x5E336C.

    for node in countries[scope->country_id]->active_modifiers (+0x648)   // {data, ?, next@+8}
        if (node->data->+8 == this->modifier (+0x40)) return true

**No date test**: an entry whose date has passed still answers true until CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers removes it. An unknown name (null, logged at load) is false unless an entry carries a null modifier.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CHasCountryModifierTrigger's table (rva 0x11F85D8), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end; the record's +0x648 comment already gives 'the modifier at +8 and a date at +0xC' per entry, which this agrees with. Wrong if +0x648 nodes were 0x10 with next elsewhere - the walk uses [node+8] as next and [node] as payload.

addresses.name: CHasRemovableMinisterTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`has_removable_minister = yes|no`: the scope's country has a minister it may dismiss.** 0x5FBFE0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5FC256.

    n = 0
    for i, p in g_government_positions (+0xC..+0x10):        // made on first use
        if (!p->slot14() || !p->isChangeable (+0x50)) continue  // slot 14: ReturnTrue on CGovernmentPosition, ReturnFalse on the null one
        m = us->ministers (+0x618) [p->index (+0x4C)]
        if (m == 0 || !m->slot8()) continue                   // slot 8: ReturnTrue on CMinister, ReturnFalse on CNullMinister
        for j, q in the same vector:
            if (ministers[q->index] == m && j != i && !q->isChangeable) goto next_i   // he also holds a fixed post
        n++
    return (n > 0) == this->value (+0x40)

A minister counts when he holds a changeable post and no unchangeable one. The inner loop re-fetches the database through the get-or-create each step.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CHasRemovableMinisterTrigger's table (rva 0x11F7E54), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end; `vtable.py CGovernmentPosition CNullGovernmentPosition` slot 14 and `CMinister CNullMinister` slot 8 are ReturnTrue/ReturnFalse. +0x50 is the Lua's `IsChangeable`. Wrong if 0x9FC218 were not the increment - it is reached only from the inner loop's `jge` exit.

addresses.name: CIsPossibleVassalTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`is_possible_vassal = TAG`: TAG is among the nations the scope's country could release.** 0x5EE320 to two `ret 4` at 0x5EE3B9 and 0x5EE3D9.

    list = CCountry::GetPossibleVassals(countries[scope->country_id])   // 0xEE320, rebuilt each call
    copy = a fresh CList<CCountryTag>, appended node by node through CList_CCountryTag_PushBack (0xBEDF0)
    found = any node of copy with id (+4) == this->target.id (+0x44)
    free copy; return found

**THIS and FROM are ignored**: the shared loader sets the flags and leaves +0x40/+0x44 at the constructor's `---`/0, and this body never reads +0x18/+0x19, so `is_possible_vassal = THIS` asks about country 0. The copy is pure overhead - three heap operations per node.
addresses.evidence: Slot 6 of CIsPossibleVassalTrigger's table (rva 0x11F8C58), single holder by `vtable.py --holding`; listing read end to end; the constructor (0x5CEAB0, the one writer of the vftable) stores `---` and 0 into +0x40/+0x44. Wrong if 0xBEDF0 did more than append - it is 0x56 bytes, `new(0x14)`, copies 8 bytes from its argument, links at the tail and bumps +8.

addresses.name: CRelationTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`relation = { who = TAG value = N }`: `us->diplomacy (+0xE28) [who.id] ->relation (+0x38) >= N * 1000`.** 0x5DDC00 to three `ret 4` at 0x5DDC80, 0x5DDD4E and 0x5DDE43, one frame.

    threshold = this->value (+0x48) * 1000
    if (arg_is_this)  id = this_scope->country_id (+0x14); if (id == 0) id = provinces[this_scope->province (+0x28)]->controller_id (+0x338)
    elif (arg_is_from) id = this_scope->from_country_id (+0x1C); if (id == 0) id = provinces[this_scope->from_province (+0x30)]->controller_id

addresses.name: CSpyMissionCountTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`spy_mission_count = { type = X value = N }`: the scope's country's spies on mission X in THIS's country, `>= N`.** 0x605B70 to the single `ret 4` at 0x605BE8.

    target = (scope->this_scope && scope->this_scope->country_id) ? this_scope->country_id : scope->country_id
    e = countries[scope->country_id]->espionage (+0x1160) + target * 0xF8
    return (int64)e->+0 * e->+(0x2C + 4 * this->mission_type (+0x40)) / 1000 >= this->value (+0x44)

Entry +0 is the spy allocation (thousandths of spies); +0x2C.. is nine dwords, one per mission type, and the product over 1000 reads as 'spies on that mission'. **The target is THIS, implicitly**: in an unnested evaluation THIS is the scope itself and the entry read is the country's own domestic one. The null test on this_scope is dead - the constructor never leaves it null.

The meaning of the nine dwords at +0x2C (`spy_mission` in the save, 'nine values an entry' in the record) as shares is inferred from the product, not from their writer.

addresses.name: DiplomacyStatus_HasUsableCasusBelli
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall DiplomacyStatus_HasUsableCasusBelli(CDiplomacyStatus* status, CCountryTag* holder, CCountryTag* target)
addresses.comment:
**Could `holder` go to war on `target` with some casus belli now.** 0x649CA0 to two `ret 0xC` at 0x649D67 and 0x649D7D, SEH frame. Makes the casus-belli-type database g_casus_belli_types (0x1685BD8) if missing, then

    for t in db->+0xC .. +0x10:                 // CCasusBelliType*, index order
        if (t->slot7() && DiplomacyStatus_CanUseCasusBelliType(t->index (+8) @EDI, status, holder, target)) return true

Slot 7 is ReturnTrue on CCasusBelliType and ReturnFalse on CNullCasusBelliType. `status` is the holder's status toward the target. Ten callers: CCasusBelliTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E7CD3), eight in the AI between 0x4A6EA8 and 0x4A8DDA, and 0x64A6E2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. `mov edi,[esi+8]` immediately before the call passes the type's +8 as the index 0x649D80 indexes the same vector with. Wrong if +8 were not the type's position - CCasusBelli +0x24 (an index) is compared against the same EDI.

addresses.comment:
**One casus belli type: held or `always`, and then its `is_valid`.** 0x649D80 to two `ret 0xC` at 0x649E8B and 0x649E9F.

    t = db[typeIndex] (db[0] when out of range)
    held = any CCasusBelli in status->casus_belli (+0x3C) with type (+0x24) == typeIndex
    if (!held && !t->always (+0x1F2)) return false
    B = CEventScope(); B.country = *holder
    A = CEventScope(); A.country = *target; A.this_scope = &B
    return t->slot6(&A)                          // CCasusBelliType::IsValid, the `is_valid` block

addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. A at [ebp-0x5C], B at [ebp-0xA4], both through CEventScope::CEventScope (0x5C1610); `mov [ebp-0x24], &B` is A+0x38; [ebp+0xC] lands at B+0x10 and [ebp+0x10] at A+0x10. addresses.name: WarGoalMap_Find
addresses.signature: void** __stdcall WarGoalMap_Find(void* map@ECX, void** out@EAX, int* key@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment: **`std::map<int, ...>::find`**, MSVC's red-black tree: head at map+4, a node's left at +0, parent +4, right +8, key +0xC, value from +0x10, `_Isnil` byte at +0x21. addresses.name: CCountry::GetPossibleVassals
addresses.comment:
**The nations this country could release, rebuilt from nothing on every call** into `possible_vassals (+0x11E0)`, which it returns. 0xEE320 to the bare `ret` at 0xEE541. The name is the game's Lua registration (Lua `GetPossiblePuppets`).

    free every node of +0x11E0; zero first, last, count
    for p in this->OwnedProvinces (+0xCF0):
        prov = provinces[p]
        if (prov->controller_id (+0x338) != this->id (+0xCA8)) continue      // must also control it
        if (prov == GetCapitalLocation(this)) continue                       // 0x17AF0
        for core in prov->cores (+0x344):                                    // {chars, id, ?, next@+0xC}
            c = countries[core.id]
            if (c->owned_province_count (+0xCF8) > 0 || core.id == this->id || core.id already listed) continue
            if (c->capital_province_id (+0xE20) is in this->OwnedProvinces) append core to +0x11E0

So a possible vassal is a country that **owns nothing**, has a core on a province this country owns and controls (not its capital), and whose **capital** this country owns (controlled or not).
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end (trap 3 checked: the one `ret` is past every branch). Eight callers. Wrong if +0x11E0 were read elsewhere as a persistent list - every call clears it first.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyStatus::HasTruce
addresses.comment:
**A truce is the 100 days after a war.** 0x6489A0 to two bare `ret` at 0x6489D7 and 0x648A70. The name is the game's Lua registration.

    if (this->war (+0x20)) return false
    last = this->war_seen_tick (+0x54)
    return last <= now && last + 0x960 > now          // 2400 hours, hard-coded

war_seen_tick is refreshed every hour the pair are at war, so the truce runs 100 days from the war's end. A pair never at war has 0 there and no truce. Six callers.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; `cmp edi,eax; jg false; add edi,0x960; cmp edi,eax; setg al`. 0x960 is an immediate, not a define read.

struct_fields.name: days_in_month
struct_fields.comment:
The one field the two CEventScope builders disagree about. RebuildCountryEventCandidates sets it to the current month's length, recomputed at 0x5C0273-0x5C02E4 from state+0xBDC with the same 0x29C55C0 epoch and 365.0 constant (0x120A550) RunHourlyTick uses and then indexed into MonthLengthTable (0x1313294); RunDailyEventPass leaves it zero (0x5C0AAD). CMeanTimeToHappen::GetChance never reads the scope, only forwards it, so this can only matter to a trigger. **The name is inference from how the value is derived, not from a use.** CEventScope is 0x48 bytes, vftable 0x11B8AEC, base CPersistent; +0x10 and +0x18 are two CCountryTags, both 0x2D2D2D ("---") at construction and only +0x10 ever filled in with the country being scoped.

**Its reader is CDateTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D3100)**, which tests `tick + this * 24 >= date`: so in RebuildCountryEventCandidates' scope `date` is already true up to a month early, and in RunDailyEventPass' scope it is exact.
